Subjective:
- Reason for visit: Pain/burning on urination, urinary frequency, and suprapubic discomfort interfering with university attendance.
- History of presenting complaint:
  • Onset “just under a week” ago (patient initially said “a few days,” later clarified).  
  • Dysuria described as burning/stinging.  
  • Urinary frequency; urgently looking for toilets.  
  • Pink-tinged urine noted today (first episode of visible blood).  
  • Achy suprapubic pain, worse during micturition; does not radiate to back or sides.  
  • Denies flank/back pain, fever, rigors, nausea, vomiting, vaginal discharge.
- Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS); no other chronic illnesses reported.
- Medications:  
  • Combined oral contraceptive pill – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Mebeverine (antispasmodic for IBS) – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social history:  
  • 1st-year university student, lives in halls with flatmate.  
  • Sexually active with long-term boyfriend; last unprotected intercourse ~1–2 weeks ago.  
  • Tried cannabis once 1½ weeks ago; occasional social alcohol; denies regular tobacco use.
- Allergies: Clindamycin (reaction not specified).

Objective:
- No vital signs or physical examination performed/documented.
- Planned investigation: Mid-stream urine (MSU) for dipstick and culture.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Dysuria/Urinary frequency with hematuria
   - Assessment: Probable uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis).
   - Differential diagnosis (if urine culture negative): urethritis (STI-related), interstitial cystitis, nephrolithiasis.
   - Investigations planned: MSU for dipstick & culture/sensitivity.
   - Treatment planned: Empiric oral antibiotic – Trimethoprim OR Nitrofurantoin 3-day course (specific agent/dose to be finalised once prescribed); maintain good hydration; paracetamol prn for pain.
   - Safety-net/Follow-up: Return sooner for fever, flank/back pain, vomiting, or symptom worsening. Routine review if no improvement after 1 week when culture results available.

2. Recreational cannabis use
   - Assessment: Single recent use; no current medical complications.
   - Treatment/Advice: Counseled to avoid further cannabis use for general health.

3. IBS – stable
   - Assessment: No change in baseline symptoms.
   - Treatment: Continue current regimen (Mebeverine); no further action today.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected: Vital signs, physical examination (abdominal, CVA tenderness), urine dip in clinic, pregnancy test, detailed allergy reaction, full medication list with doses, smoking status for tobacco explicitly recorded, family history detail.  
● Internal conflicts: Symptom duration stated as “a few days,” later “just under a week” – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear, minimal background noise; no significant inaudible sections.
